skill.name: monet-palette-photo
skill.description: Transform a user-supplied photograph through source-responsive Monet-inspired color, light, brushwork, edge logic, and optional sparse social-media art direction. Route among full, subject-only, atmospheric, zine-hybrid, and distilled treatments. Zine Hybrid can preserve one prominent original-pixel anchor cutout beside one painted color-event cutout with 30–60% quiet paper, and the accepted result can optionally be packaged as a warm comparison poster.

identity.promise: Preserve a photograph's identity and spatial logic while translating explicitly selected regions into source-responsive Monet-inspired color, light, brushwork, and perceptual structure.
identity.output_medium: one generated or edited raster image, or an original-over-generated comparison poster, plus a concise routing and art-direction rationale
positive_identity: painted zones are chosen from light, atmosphere, reflection, color variation, and edge instability
palette, brush, and edge behavior remain traceable to the supplied photograph
mutually incompatible source-pixel policies are isolated by mode
a sparse social profile can reduce detail and expose source-derived quiet fields without changing mode
comparison-poster delivery is deterministic and separate from image generation
Zine Cutout Isolation retains exactly one original-pixel photographic anchor with primary recognition weight and one separately traceable painted carrier while keeping 30–60% quiet paper
anti_identity: black-shadow default with no chromatic variation
random brush texture unrelated to surface, depth, or light
invented water lilies, bridges, gardens, flowers, or sunsets
dense collage filler that competes with the semantic anchor
generative recreation of the original-over-generated poster layout
arbitrary decorative cutouts or surviving scenery in a two-cutout isolation result
a regenerated likeness presented as a preserved photographic anchor

use_when: the user wants a photograph reinterpreted through Monet-inspired color and brush logic
the user wants only light, atmosphere, reflection, a subject, or selected regions transformed
the user wants a photo-and-paint zine hybrid or a distilled impressionist reconstruction
the user wants only a photographic anchor and the main Monet color carrier cut out on blank paper
the user wants a social-ready sparse treatment with extracted shapes and deliberate negative space
the user wants the original above the generated result on a warm comparison poster
do_not_use_when: the user wants a generic oil-paint filter with no selective art direction
the user needs a text-heavy editorial page or commercial key visual
the user has not supplied a photograph
examples: Keep the person photographic and turn only the water reflection and sunlit foliage into impressionist paint.
Use Full Impression at M3 while preserving the street geometry and figure identities.
Distill this rainy scene into an M4 painting with no source pixels and a sparse social profile.
Put the original above the generated result on a warm 4:5 comparison poster.
Cut out the person as photography and the reflected-light carrier as paint; remove everything else to quiet paper.

input_kinds: optional exact short title or caption
optional presentation profile, Zine strategy, and delivery layout
optional exact comparison-poster background color or destination ratio

authority: observed light, atmosphere, and native color relations
palette, brush, light, edge, and QA requirements

precedence: the selected mode's source-pixel policy outranks aesthetic preference
source identity and decisive spatial relations outrank painterly texture
presentation profile controls density but never changes the selected mode's source-pixel policy
delivery layout operates only on accepted raster panels and never changes either panel
cutout_isolation requires two distinct source regions, an original-pixel identity lock, and 30–60% quiet paper
observed light and surface behavior outrank generic Monet associations
user-supplied exact text outranks authored wording
allowed_transformations: source-responsive color decomposition and chromatic shadow construction
surface-, depth-, and light-directed brush translation
mode-specific preservation, simplification, line reduction, paper removal, or spatial recomposition
controlled edge softening, breaking, and loss
source-derived silhouette, contour, field, rhythm, or cutout abstraction
two-mask isolation of one photographic anchor and one Monet-painted carrier with the inverse removed to paper
forbidden_inventions: unrequested people, objects, scenery, weather, reflections, or architecture
water lilies, bridges, gardens, flowers, sunsets, and other painter-associated clichés absent from the source
invented dates, coordinates, labels, quotations, credits, signatures, or watermarks
uniform filter texture across every surface and depth layer
invented poster labels, metadata, shadows, tape, or decorative props
extra collage scraps, linework, scenery, or arbitrary shapes in a Cutout Isolation result
handling: inspect the supplied photograph directly and do not browse for substitute imagery
send only the final prompt and required source image to the configured generation or editing service
do not save, search, publish, or redistribute the source unless the user asks
disclose external-service use briefly after generation

fields.name: mode
fields.question: Which single transformation mode controls source-pixel retention and visual treatment?

fields.name: presentation_profile
fields.question: Should the artwork use immersive field coverage or sparse social-media density?
fields.default: Use explicit cues, then the selected mode's profile default.

fields.name: zine_strategy
fields.question: For Zine Hybrid, should photo and paint remain an integrated sparse scene or become exactly two isolated cutouts?
fields.default: not_applicable outside Zine Hybrid; integrated_field for a generic Zine request; cutout_isolation when the user asks to keep only the anchor and carrier.

fields.name: zine_cutout_plan
fields.question: When Cutout Isolation is selected, what are the exact anchor scope, recognition features, original-pixel identity lock, primary scale, Monet carrier, source evidence, boundary logic, surviving relation, and 30–60% quiet paper field?

fields.name: semantic_anchor
fields.question: Which subject or relationship makes this photograph meaningful?

fields.name: spatial_invariants
fields.question: Which positions, axes, directions, scales, or overlaps must survive?

fields.name: protected_elements
fields.question: Which faces, hands, logos, text, identity features, or structures must not drift?

fields.name: impressionability_candidates
fields.question: Which zones score highest for light, atmosphere, reflection, color variation, and edge instability?

fields.name: transformation_map
fields.question: Which zones are painted, preserved, simplified, drawn, or removed into negative space?

fields.name: light_card
fields.question: What are the observed direction, temperature, intensity, diffusion, surface interaction, highlights, shadows, and reflection relation?

fields.name: palette_families
fields.question: Which source-responsive dominant, light, warm/cool counter, reflection, and chromatic-dark families construct the Monet zones?

fields.name: brush_map
fields.question: Which brush family, direction, scale, and density belongs to each painted zone?

fields.name: edge_map
fields.question: Which zones use L1 defined, L2 soft, L3 broken, or L4 lost edges?

fields.name: shape_abstraction
fields.question: For sparse social work, what semantic minimum, source shapes, retain/merge/omit/transform/expose actions, graphic grammar, density budget, and thumbnail anchor control reduction?
fields.default: Null for immersive; required and validated for sparse_social.

fields.name: background_treatment
fields.question: Should the support remain photographic, simplified, line-based, or paper-like?
fields.default: Select from the mode and source; background must visually defer.

fields.name: visible_text
fields.question: What exact short title or caption, if any, should appear?

decision_priority: preserve the semantic anchor and required identity
obey the selected mode's source-pixel policy
select a presentation profile without altering source-pixel policy
for Zine Hybrid, select integrated_field or cutout_isolation before assigning regions
choose zones through Impressionability Map evidence
let light control palette, brush, and edge behavior
for sparse work, reduce detail through one source-derived graphic grammar and protect quiet fields
for cutout isolation, retain exactly one original-pixel photo anchor at primary or balanced prominence, one painted carrier, 30–60% paper, and delete every other region
remove unplanned transformation before adding texture
reasoning_chain: select one mode and one presentation profile
resolve one Zine strategy when applicable
build the transformation and preservation map
choose background, transition, and optional sparse shape system
inspect against Monet authenticity and thumbnail QA
optionally compose an accepted original-over-generated poster and run delivery QA

branches.name: Full Impression
branches.when: the user explicitly wants the complete photograph repainted
branches.contract: retain source identity and composition but no source pixels

branches.name: Subject Monetization
branches.when: the user wants the primary subject painted against a reduced non-photographic background
branches.contract: retain subject identity semantically but no source pixels by default

branches.name: Atmospheric Monetization
branches.when: the user wants the anchor photographic and light, air, water, reflection, or unstable edges painted

branches.name: Zine Hybrid
branches.when: the user wants truthful photo material combined with paint, paper, or restrained linework
branches.contract: partial source-pixel preservation is required; integrated_field remains the default, while cutout_isolation requires one original-pixel photographic anchor at primary or balanced prominence, one painted carrier, and 30–60% quiet paper

branches.name: Distilled Monet
branches.when: the user wants a freer semantic and structural distillation with no photography
branches.contract: no source pixels; preserve only selected semantic, spatial, light, and color anchors

must_have: one semantic anchor and one dominant painted event
source-responsive color decomposition with chromatic darks
brush direction tied to surface, depth, motion, reflection, or light
edge hierarchy tied to identity and atmosphere
a source-derived transition or a fully repainted no-pixel contract
for sparse social work, one primary graphic grammar and deliberate quiet fields
for cutout isolation, exactly two source-derived active pieces linked by one preserved source relation, with the original-pixel anchor immediately recognizable
variable_slots: primary and up to two secondary Monet zones
silhouette, contour, field, rhythm, and cutout graphic grammars
anti_patterns: whole-image filter when a selective mode is chosen
every edge equally blurred or equally sharp
zine devices overpowering paint and source identity
equal detail across the frame or several competing collage clusters
poster layout generated by an image model instead of deterministic composition
three or more pieces, auxiliary linework, or residual scenery in a two-cutout isolation result

composition.aspect_ratio_policy: preserve source orientation by default; use another ratio only for an explicit output destination
layout_families: source composition retained with selective painted zones
photographic anchor plus source-derived atmospheric paint field
subject-led painted form against simplified, line, or paper support
asymmetric zine hybrid linked by a real light, gaze, path, or reflection axis
distilled broad-field reconstruction with two to four source anchors
sparse source-derived active cluster surrounded by blank or low-information fields
one photographic anchor cutout and one painted carrier cutout separated by quiet paper
warm comparison poster with truthful original above and accepted artwork below
hierarchy: one Monet zone is the dominant perceptual event
secondary painted zones support the same event
composition.negative_space_policy: use quiet source, simplified color, paper, haze, water, wall, sky, or fully painted low-information fields to separate ideas; sparse_social normally targets 45–85% quiet area, while cutout_isolation uses 30–60% true paper so the anchor and carrier remain substantial
composition.source_allocation: determined by the selected mode and transformation card; never use a mechanical half-and-half split

color.policy: build five to nine source-responsive color families or roles around observed light, warm/cool counterpoint, reflection, and chromatic darks

typography.policy: use no visible text by default; allow one exact two-to-four-word title or one very short caption
typography.exact_text_strategy: generate art without text and composite deterministically when spelling is production-critical

material.policy: use matte, surface-responsive painterly behavior in transformed zones and flat presentation for hybrid work
roles: optional restrained paper or line support
two source-derived flat cutouts when isolation is selected
constraints: paper depth remains flat and subordinate

field_order: task, mode, strength, presentation profile, applicable Zine strategy, and output orientation
transformation, preservation, reduction, and discard map
optional Cutout Isolation plan with original-pixel anchor scope, recognition features, primary scale, exact two-piece boundaries, surviving relation, and inverse-to-paper deletion
exact short text or no text
prompt_compiler.visible_pixel_rule: Include only source-specific directions that affect the visible result or required tool behavior; keep scores, JSON, file paths, provenance, and internal analysis out of the render prompt. Keep comparison-poster layout out of the render prompt because it is deterministic post-processing.
negative_constraints: no painting outside the validated mask in partial modes
no uniform oil-paint filter, universal pastel palette, or flat black-shadow default
no random brush behavior, hard digital split, or invented Monet motif
no text other than exact user-supplied short copy
for cutout_isolation, no third piece, supporting grammar, residual scene, or painted paper field
tool_requirements: a reference-image generation or editing tool
regional editing, masking, or deterministic compositing for partial-preservation modes
visual inspection capability for result QA when available
prompt_compiler.fallback: return the validated card, complete English render prompt, zone/mask plan, and parameters while stating which fidelity capability is unavailable

pre_generation: one mode is selected and compatible with the source-pixel policy
the source photograph has been inspected
semantic anchor, protected elements, and spatial invariants are explicit
Impressionability scores and zone assignments are valid
light, palette, brush, edge, background, transition, and text fields are resolved
the Transformation Card passes the bundled validator
sparse_social resolves a semantic minimum, one primary grammar, density budgets, quiet fields, and thumbnail anchor
cutout_isolation resolves two distinct source regions, exact card mappings, original-pixel identity lock, three to eight recognition features, one surviving relation, and a 30–60% paper field
comparison_poster resolves a Social Output Card only after artwork approval
result_checks: semantic anchor and spatial relationship remain readable
only planned zones are transformed and source-pixel rules are respected
light changes local color and chromatic shadows remain colored
warm/cool variation and reflection relationships are visible where planned
brush direction and scale respond to surface, depth, and light
edge hierarchy and transition behave as planned
background and zine devices remain subordinate
sparse social artwork has one active cluster, deliberate quiet fields, and thumbnail legibility
cutout isolation has exactly one original-pixel photographic anchor piece with intact recognition features and one painted carrier piece with no background leakage
comparison poster preserves both panels and visible background spacing
no invented motif, object, weather, reflection, metadata, or signature appears
repair_dimensions: cutout count, subject recognition, source-pixel provenance, relation, or discarded-background leakage

default_deliverables: one generated or edited raster image, or the composed comparison poster when requested
selected mode, M1–M4 strength, presentation profile, and applicable Zine strategy
one concise rationale naming the Monet zones and decisive perceptual relationship
brief external-service disclosure when a source image was sent for generation or editing
on_request: standalone artwork in addition to a poster
output_contract.failure_behavior: state the unavailable capability or named failed QA dimension and return the complete prompt and zone plan without claiming an unperformed or unsuccessful transformation

license_notes: The visual-system requirements were derived from a user-supplied design conversation and rewritten as original skill instructions.
The skill describes Monet-inspired color and perceptual principles without bundling third-party artwork, prompt text, or example images.
Public zine skills were consulted for high-level architecture and visual-design patterns only. Their wording, assets, examples, and layouts were not copied.
Repository-specific licenses remain authoritative for the consulted sources; this skill stores only original summaries and source URLs.
provenance.originality_statement: This implementation independently structures the supplied concept into mode routing, profile routing, source-derived shape abstraction, deterministic comparison-poster delivery, schemas, prompt compilation, and observable QA.

assumptions.value: mode-dependent: sparse_social for Subject, Zine, and Distilled; immersive for Full and Atmospheric
4:5 at 1080 px wide, source-derived warm background, contained panels, no labels
integrated_field for generic Zine Hybrid; cutout_isolation only from explicit keep-two-and-remove-rest intent
